items.answer: Dominion is authority delegated by God, not ownership; stewardship uses it with care and accountability because the earth still belongs to its Creator.
The Lord confirmed to Isaac the same promises given to Abraham, His presence, descendants, land and blessing to the nations, based on God's faithfulness and not Isaac's ability.
Everyone bears God's image, giving unearned and permanent dignity, and everyone is also touched by sin in every part; both are true together.
Uniformity means everyone doing everything the same way, while unity is oneness in the essentials of the faith that allows diversity in secondary matters.
The risen Jesus, beginning at Moses and all the Prophets, explained in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself, so every part of Scripture points to Christ.
The questions are what the speaker actually meant, whether a flat literal reading produces an absurdity, and whether it is a figure of speech or literal reality.
The first preachers had heard Jesus personally and received the Spirit at Pentecost at the start of the age, which no later century can repeat.
Justin Martyr wrote the First Apology answering slanders, and Tertullian gave Western theology its Latin vocabulary, including the word Trinity, three persons in one substance.
The Counter-Reformation was Catholicism's reply to the Reformation; Trent corrected real abuses yet reaffirmed Catholic doctrine against Protestant teaching.
Carey answered hyper-Calvinists who said the Commission was only for the apostles, arguing in his Enquiry that Christians must use means to evangelize the world.

items.answer: Luke opens Acts by saying his Gospel recorded all that Jesus 'began' to do and teach until His ascension, so Acts is the second volume of the same story. In Acts the risen and ascended Lord keeps working, now through His Spirit-empowered Church rather than in His earthly body. The book even lacks a formal ending because the work is not finished. This teaches that Christ's ministry did not stop at the ascension; He is still acting today through believers filled with His Spirit, and we are living in that long second volume.

Second, divided tongues as of fire rested on each person; fire marked God's presence in the burning bush, the pillar of fire, and the altar on Carmel, and now it rests on individuals instead of a building, showing the temple is being relocated into God's people. Third, they spoke God's wonders in languages they had never learned, so pilgrims heard the gospel in their own dialects; this looks back to Babel, where God confused the languages, and reverses it.

What was scattered in judgment is gathered in grace, around Jesus rather than around human pride. items.answer: Peter first answers the mockers: these men are not drunk, since it is only nine in the morning. Second, he explains the event from Joel: this is the promised outpouring of the Spirit on all flesh. Third, he preaches Jesus: approved by miracles, delivered up and crucified by God's deliberate plan, raised from the dead as David foretold in Psalm 16, and now exalted at God's right hand, from where He poured out the Spirit. The central claim is Acts 2:36, that God has made this Jesus whom they crucified both Lord and Christ. When the crowd was cut to the heart, he called them to repent and be baptized in Jesus' name for the remission of sins and receive the gift of the Spirit, and about three thousand believed.

items.answer: Acts 2:42 shows the Word (the apostles' doctrine), the family (fellowship), the table (breaking of bread), and the throne room (prayer), and if any one is dropped the church becomes something other than the New Testament church. In my view the modern church most often neglects prayer. Many churches have strong teaching programs and social events, but corporate prayer meetings are small or missing, because prayer is slow, unseen, and does not fit our instant, busy culture. Yet Pentecost came after ten days of prayer, and revivals like the Hebrides began in prayer, so neglecting it cuts the church off from the Spirit's power.

items.answer: In Acts 1:8 Jesus promises power when the Spirit comes and says the disciples will be His witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth. That verse works as the book's table of contents. So the book traces the gospel moving outward in widening circles from a Jewish center to all nations.

items.answer: Gamaliel, a respected Pharisee and Saul's teacher, calmed the Sanhedrin when they wanted to kill the apostles. He pointed to Theudas and Judas of Galilee, whose movements collapsed after they died, and argued that a merely human movement would burn out, but one from God could not be stopped, and opposing it would mean fighting against God. Luke presents him as wise, but nothing in the text shows he became a believer; his advice was cautious neutrality, and the council still flogged the apostles. His caution teaches that discernment means taking time to see what bears God's fruit and fearing to oppose God, though true discernment must eventually lead to a decision about Jesus rather than permanent fence-sitting.

items.answer: When the Greek-speaking widows were neglected in the daily food distribution, the Twelve did not ignore the complaint or try to do everything themselves. They said it was not right for them to leave the word of God to serve tables, so they had the congregation choose seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and wisdom, and laid hands on them. This let the apostles give themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word, while a real need was met promptly. It models delegation that respects different callings, involves the congregation, insists on spiritual qualifications even for practical tasks, and produces growth; two of the Seven, Stephen and Philip, became a martyr and an evangelist.

Mitsuo Fuchida led the attack on Pearl Harbor and lived as an enemy of Christ, until a tract by Jacob DeShazer, an American prisoner who had been converted by reading Jesus' words 'Father, forgive them,' led him to read the Bible and meet Jesus. Several strategic lessons emerge. First, follow the Spirit's guidance, even through closed doors, as with the Macedonian vision. Second, adapt the setting while keeping the message: Paul preached to women at a riverside, to a jailer in prison, to Jews in synagogues, to philosophers in the marketplace, and to the council on Mars Hill, always proclaiming Jesus and the resurrection. Third, build households and local leaders, like Lydia, the jailer, and Crispus, and partner with lay workers like Aquila and Priscilla. Fourth, endure suffering with worship and stay where God has many people, as in Corinth. Finally, train believers to be Bereans who test teaching by Scripture.

He did not use his rights all the time to avoid suffering for Christ, but he invoked them when due process and the law itself were being violated. items.answer: Throughout Acts the gospel is costly. Stephen was stoned, James was killed with the sword, Peter was jailed, and Paul was beaten with rods, lashed, stoned and left for dead at Lystra, shipwrecked, and finally chained in Rome. Financially, the Ephesian believers burned magic books worth fifty thousand pieces of silver, and the silversmiths lost income. Health-and-wealth theology teaches that faithful believers will be spared trouble and blessed with prosperity, but Acts shows the most faithful servants suffering the most. As the lesson says, being saved is not the same as being safe; God promises storm-tested arrivals, not storm-free voyages, so a cheap gospel is not the gospel of Acts.

items.answer: Premillennialism holds that Christ returns before a literal future thousand-year reign on earth; it comes in historic and dispensational forms and was held by Justin Martyr and Irenaeus. Postmillennialism expects Christ to return after a long golden age in which the gospel gradually wins the nations, as Jonathan Edwards and the Puritans held. Amillennialism sees the thousand years as symbolic of Christ's present reign from heaven between His two comings, the view of Augustine, Luther and Calvin. The unit treats them even-handedly: sincere Bible-loving believers have held each for centuries, none is a test of fellowship, and all agree on Christ's bodily return, the resurrection and the final judgment.

items.answer: En Mileto Pablo llamó a los ancianos de Éfeso y les recordó cómo había servido con humildad, lágrimas y pruebas, enseñando públicamente y por las casas. 'Todo el consejo de Dios' significa que no retuvo ninguna parte de la verdad revelada, incluso lo difícil o impopular, sino que anunció todo lo necesario para la salvación y la vida piadosa. Les encargó cuidar de sí mismos y del rebaño, que Dios ganó con su propia sangre, contra lobos rapaces que vendrían de afuera y aun de entre ellos mismos. 'Amonestar con lágrimas noche y día a cada uno' describe el corazón del verdadero pastorado: un cuidado constante, personal y compasivo por cada alma. Como Moody después del incendio de Chicago, el pastor debe predicar con urgencia y lágrimas.

items.answer: Después de la cena Jesús fue a Getsemaní, oró en agonía y se entregó a la voluntad del Padre. Judas, uno de los suyos, guió a soldados con antorchas y armas para arrestarlo, una traición profunda de un amigo de confianza. items.answer: Cuando Pilato preguntó: '¿A vuestro Rey he de crucificar?', los principales sacerdotes respondieron: 'No tenemos más rey que César', y Jesús fue llevado al Gólgota. items.answer: El Evangelio de Juan está construido como un juicio: la afirmación es que Jesús es Dios en carne, y Juan llama testigo tras testigo para que el lector, como un jurado, pese la evidencia y dicte un veredicto. Juan 20:31 dice que escribió para que creamos que Jesús es el Cristo, el Hijo de Dios, y tengamos vida en su nombre. Según la ley judía, un asunto se establecía por dos o tres testigos, porque uno solo puede equivocarse. Jesús presenta muchos más de dos, y todos concuerdan, de modo que el lector queda sin excusa.

items.answer: Una parábola es una historia terrenal con un significado celestial, y a la vez revela y oculta. Cuando los discípulos preguntaron por qué las usaba, Jesús dijo que a ellos les era dado saber los misterios del reino, pero a los demás no. Al corazón hambriento que quiere entender, la historia le abre la verdad; al corazón endurecido que ya se apartó, sigue siendo un enigma, cumpliendo las palabras de Isaías: 'Viendo no ven, y oyendo no oyen.' items.answer: Conformarse es ser apretado desde afuera al molde del mundo. Transformarse, del griego metamorphoō, es ser cambiado desde adentro por la renovación del entendimiento. La oruga no se convierte en mariposa al ser presionada en un molde con forma de mariposa, sino por un cambio interior, y así es el crecimiento cristiano. Ambos verbos están en presente, de modo que la vida cristiana es una lucha diaria entre la presión del mundo y la obra continua del Espíritu.

items.answer: The difference, as I understand it from the lesson, is that literal interpretation means taking the words in the sense that the author actually intended, and sometimes the author intended a figure of speech, so when Jesus says "I am the door" we read it literally by taking His intended figure. Literalistic interpretation is different, because it flattens everything down to the bare physical meaning of the words and ignores that the author may have meant a figure, so it would make Jesus a piece of wood. items.answer: The four councils in order are these. Nicaea in 325, which condemned Arius and affirmed that the Son is homoousios, of the same substance as the Father. Then Constantinople in 381, which confirmed Nicaea and confessed the full deity of the Holy Spirit, finishing the doctrine of the Trinity. Then Ephesus in 431, which condemned Nestorius and affirmed Mary as theotokos. And last Chalcedon in 451, which defined that Christ is one person in two natures, divine and human.
